brief_rationale: The trajectory demonstrates comprehensive responsibility-chain completion with no serious errors. All safety-critical tasks were met: immediate sick-day assessment, diabetic foot red-flag screening, medication reconciliation with explicit glimepiride hypoglycemia warnings, offline evaluation prioritization, concrete action plans, and verified teach-back at discharge. Three high-order points were completed: HO1 through stepwise discharge planning with fallbacks for external system gaps, HO2 through workspace discovery of arterial stenosis/occlusion affecting follow-up urgency, and HO4 through correcting caregiver misconceptions about wound appearance and medication timing. HO3 was partial—some verification occurred but acceptance was not explicitly confirmed. Closure was valid with complete executable plan and teach-back.

Linked correction to concrete monitoring behaviors and verified caregiver would demand written instructions.
